questions.q: What is the main difference between a simple sentence and a complex sentence?
questions.a: A simple sentence has one independent clause, while a complex sentence includes at least one dependent clause. A wrong answer suggests the student confuses them with compound sentences or does not recognize what a "complete thought" is.

questions.q: Read this: "Although Prabhat felt nervous, he played the game." Is this a simple or complex sentence? Why?
questions.a: It is a complex sentence because "Although Prabhat felt nervous" cannot stand alone as a sentence. A wrong answer reveals the student thinks the presence of two verbs automatically makes it a "simple" sentence.

questions.q: Turn the simple sentence "Surya smiled" into a complex sentence by adding a dependent clause.
questions.a: Example: "When the match ended, Surya smiled." This requires the student to attach a dependent thought (using a subordinate conjunction) to the main clause. A wrong answer shows the student does not understand how to create a dependent clause.

questions.q: Analyze the sentence: "Because it was raining, we stopped the game." Identify the dependent clause and the independent clause.
questions.a: Dependent: "Because it was raining"; Independent: "we stopped the game." A wrong answer shows the student cannot identify which part of the sentence provides a complete meaning.

questions.q: Critique this sentence: "I went home because." Is this a complete complex sentence? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is incomplete because "because" requires a reason to follow it to make it a proper dependent clause. A wrong answer indicates the student does not understand that dependent clauses must contain both a subject and a verb.

questions.q: Create a complex sentence about playing a sport in your school playground.
questions.a: Acceptable answers follow the pattern: [Dependent clause] + [Independent clause] or vice versa (e.g., "If we finish our homework, we will play cricket"). Poor answers lack a dependent clause or are just two simple sentences joined incorrectly.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A simple sentence ______ one independent clause (a complete thought), while a complex sentence combines one independent clause with a dependent clause (a group of words that needs the independent clause to make sense).
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are telling your ______ about your day at school.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify a simple vs. complex sentence and write one example of each correctly.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: ______ you are telling your friend about your day at school.
